title: Latvian braid mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with a two-colour Latvian braid at the cuff.
excerpt: Full mittens with a two-colour Latvian braid at the cuff, worked in DK wool in the round. The braid is a decorative purl-row technique that creates a twisted band. Gusseted thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: The Latvian braid is documented in Lizbeth Upitis, Latvian Mittens (1981), and appears in published folk-knitting collections at the National Museum of Latvia. The braid technique itself appears in Estonian and Latvian knitwear traditions from at least the 19th century, all now out of copyright.

glossaryTerms.definition: A decorative two-colour band worked in the round by purling alternate stitches in each colour, swapping the yarn positions between each stitch so the two yarns twist around each other. The result is a braided or twisted ridge that sits on the right side of the fabric.

A thumb opening made by increasing a wedge of stitches over several rounds at the thumb position, then placing them on waste yarn. The gusset gives a better anatomical fit at the base of the thumb than an afterthought thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.
An increase worked by lifting the horizontal strand between two stitches with the left needle and knitting into the back of it. M1L lifts from left to right; M1R lifts from right to left.

The Latvian braid is worked by purling two rounds with both colours, swapping which yarn sits in front between each stitch so the yarns twist into a visible cord. One braid round twists the yarns one way; the following braid round reverses the twist to lock the cord. The main hand is plain stocking stitch with a thumb gusset worked on the palm side. Budget about 100 g of MC (220 m / 240 yards) and 20 g of CC (44 m / 48 yards), both DK weight.

items.name: CC (contrast colour)
items.qty: 20 g (about 44 m / 48 yards) of the same yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers

items.name: Waste yarn

content.text: 22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. Swatch in stocking stitch with MC only.

attrs.heading: Two braid rounds worked in the round

items.name: Braid round 1 (forward twist)
items.qty: Bring both yarns to front. *P1 with MC, bring MC over CC to back, p1 with CC, bring CC over MC to back*; repeat to end. The yarns twist forward with each pair of stitches.

items.name: Braid round 2 (reverse twist)
items.qty: Bring both yarns to front. *P1 with MC, bring MC under CC to back, p1 with CC, bring CC under MC to back*; repeat to end. The yarns untwist to lock the braid.

content.text: Work both braid rounds consecutively at the cuff to create one locked braid band. Keeping both yarns in front for the entire braid section makes the purl rows easier to manage. After the braid, drop CC to the inside and continue in MC only.
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round using
. Work 10 (10, 12) rounds of 2x2 rib in MC.
Join CC. Work braid round 1 (forward twist), then braid round 2 (reverse twist). Drop CC to inside. Work 1 knit round in MC to reset the fabric.
Work 4 rounds in MC stocking stitch.
Place gusset markers around the first 2 stitches of the round. Increase round: SM,

, k2, M1L, SM, knit to end. Work 2 plain rounds. Repeat the increase round every 3rd round until the gusset holds 14 (16, 18) stitches. Place gusset stitches on waste yarn. Cast on 2 stitches over the gap. Continue in MC stocking stitch for 22 (24, 26) rounds.

Place a marker at the midpoint (between stitches 20/21, 22/23, or 24/25). Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Return gusset stitches to needle. Pick up 2 stitches from the bridging cast-on. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Decrease as for the mitten top. Draw through and close.

Braid looks uneven: the yarns were not consistently swapped between each stitch. Work slowly and check that the outgoing yarn goes over (round 1) or under (round 2) the incoming yarn on every single stitch.
Braid puckers the fabric: the braid yarns were pulled too tightly. Hold the braid stitches slightly looser than the stockinette rows, or use a needle one size larger for the two braid rounds only.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Wet-block and pin flat to open the braid.
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Block after washing to keep the braid flat.
Traditional Latvian mittens combine a braid cuff with a dense colourwork hand. The Selbu-style mittens pattern uses a similar two-colour structure on the full mitten body.
